## 1. Who we are

The website **metiv.org** ("the Site") is operated by Metiv - The Israel Psychotrauma Center. For any privacy inquiry: [info@metiv.org](mailto:info@metiv.org).

Using the Site constitutes acceptance of this policy and of the [Terms of Use](/terms-of-use). This policy is written in a general form of address and applies to all genders.

## 2. What we do not collect

The Site has no registration, user accounts, forms or payments. We do not ask for your name, phone number, address or email, we do not accept file uploads, and we do not sell or rent information to anyone.

**Your answers to the self-screening questionnaire and your score are calculated in your browser only.** They are not sent to any server and are not stored by us - we do not know who filled out the questionnaire or what result they got.

**We do not collect or store chat messages** - they are sent to third-party providers solely to generate the response (Section 4).

## 3. What we do collect

* **Browser preferences** - the interface language and the path you chose. They are stored on your device only, are not sent to us, and can be deleted by clearing the Site's data.
* **Technical server data** - our hosting providers log your IP address, browser type and the page loaded, for operational and security purposes.

**The Site does not set cookies of its own**, and it has no Google Analytics, advertising pixels or cross-site tracking.

## 4. The chat and artificial intelligence

The chat is an automated assistant based on a language model (AI), not a person.

**We do not collect or store chat messages.** We have no conversation history and cannot recover what was written. Messages are sent to third-party providers - **Cloudflare and Google (Gemini)** - solely to generate the response, and for this purpose they are also transferred outside Israel. How these providers handle the data is governed by their own policies (Section 5). We do not use conversations to train models.

**Do not enter identifying details in the chat** - yours or anyone else's. Responses are generated automatically, may be wrong, and are not medical advice or a diagnosis.

**Distress detection:** The Site runs an automated mechanism that detects expressions suggesting self-harm and displays emergency numbers. It may miss things, **no person reads the conversations**, and no one is alerted. The Site is not an emergency service or a helpline.

**In immediate distress: ERAN 1201 · MDA 101 · Police 100.**

## 5. Providers

Render (hosting), Cloudflare (chat server and network protection), Google (Gemini - generating chat responses). Each has its own privacy policy: [Render](https://render.com/privacy) · [Cloudflare](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/) · [Google](https://policies.google.com/privacy).

Beyond this, we do not transfer information to anyone, unless required to do so by law or court order.

## 6. Retention and deletion

Questionnaire answers and chat messages are not stored by us at all. Browser preferences remain on your device until you delete them. Server logs are kept by the providers according to their own policies, usually for a short period.

## 7. Your rights

Under the Protection of Privacy Law, 5741-1981, you have the right to review, correct and delete information stored about you. Because we do not collect identifying details, in most cases we hold no information that can be linked to you. Inquiries: [info@metiv.org](mailto:info@metiv.org).

## 8. Age

The Site is intended for people aged 18 and over. Minors should use it with a parent or guardian. We do not knowingly collect personal information from minors.

## 9. External links

The Site links to external websites and services. We are not responsible for their content or their privacy policies.

## 10. Changes, governing law and jurisdiction

We may update this policy; the date of the latest update appears at the top of the page, and continued use constitutes acceptance. This policy is governed by the laws of the State of Israel, and the competent courts of the Tel Aviv-Jaffa District have exclusive jurisdiction.

## 1. Acceptance of the terms

These terms apply to the use of the website **metiv.org** ("the Site"), operated by Metiv - The Israel Psychotrauma Center. Browsing the Site or using the questionnaire or the chat constitutes acceptance of these terms and of the [Privacy Policy](/privacy-policy). If you do not agree, please do not use the Site.

These terms are written in a general form of address and apply to all genders.

## 2. What the service is

The Site is a collection of information and self-help tools on post-traumatic stress (PTSD). It is **free** to use and has no registration, accounts, subscriptions or payments - there is nothing to renew or cancel. The Site **does not provide treatment** and does not connect users with therapists. Nothing in the Site's content makes it a clinical service.

## 3. Medical disclaimer

**The Site does not provide medical, mental health, legal or insurance advice.** The content is general information only, not tailored to your situation, and using the Site **does not create a therapist-patient relationship**. Do not rely on the Site to diagnose a medical condition, or to start, stop or change any treatment - including medication.

**The self-screening questionnaire is not a diagnosis** but a screening tool only: a high result is not a diagnosis, and a low result does not rule out a problem. Information about rights is general, may change and is not legal advice - verify it with the relevant official body.

## 4. Emergencies

**The Site is not an emergency service and is not monitored by a person.** No one reads what is written on it in real time, and no one is alerted as a result of its use.

In immediate danger, at risk of self-harm or with suicidal thoughts - reach out now: **ERAN 1201 · MDA 101 · Police 100 · or the nearest emergency room.**

## 5. The automated chat

The chat is an AI-based assistant, not a person. Responses are generated automatically, may be wrong or incomplete, and should not be relied on. The chat answers only on topics covered on the Site. **Chat messages are not collected or stored by us** - they are sent to third-party providers solely to generate the response (see the [Privacy Policy](/privacy-policy)). **Do not enter identifying details in it.** Use is rate-limited, and the chat may not be used to produce offensive or illegal content or to circumvent the system's limits.

## 6. Age

The Site is intended for people aged 18 and over. Use by minors requires the supervision and consent of a parent or guardian.

## 7. Prohibited uses

You may not copy, distribute or republish the Site's content except for personal, non-commercial use. You may not reverse engineer the Site, scrape its content automatically, run bots, circumvent limits or security measures, attempt to access restricted areas of the Site, overload or disrupt the Site's operation, use it in an illegal or harmful way, or impersonate any person or entity. We may block access for anyone who violates this section, without prior notice.

Copyright in the Site's content, design and code belongs to Metiv - The Israel Psychotrauma Center and/or to the rights holders on its behalf. You may view, save and print the content **for personal, non-commercial use only**. Any other use - including republication, commercial use or use for training models - requires prior written permission.

## 9. Liability

The Site is provided **"AS IS"**, with no commitment to availability, accuracy or error-free operation, and without warranty of any kind. To the maximum extent permitted by law, we will not be liable for any damage - direct or indirect - arising from the use of the Site, reliance on its content, questionnaire results, chat responses or the use of external websites it links to. **Nothing in the above limits liability that cannot be limited by law.**

You agree to indemnify us for any claim or expense we incur as a result of your violation of these terms.

We may change these terms, the Site or its availability, and limit or block access - at any time and without prior notice. The date of the latest update appears at the top of the page, and continued use after that constitutes acceptance. These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Israel, and the competent courts of the Tel Aviv-Jaffa District have exclusive jurisdiction. [info@metiv.org](mailto:info@metiv.org) · See also the [Privacy Policy](/privacy-policy).

## Personal and national trauma and its impact on organizations

The October 7 disaster and the Iron Swords war have exposed, and continue to expose, many people to severe traumatic events experienced on a personal, family, community and national level. Israeli society now has many people wounded physically and emotionally in the war, bereaved families, and friends who have experienced loss. Many people in the country are in a state of heightened alertness in the face of the ongoing security situation.

Trauma does not stay contained in the therapy room. Often, trauma survivors' encounters with service providers unintentionally trigger a renewed traumatic experience. Cumbersome and unclear bureaucratic processes, a cold or dismissive attitude from service providers, security checks - all of these can stir up feelings of lack of control, a reliving of experiences of humiliation or rejection, and can bring a person who has experienced trauma to frustration, rage and loss of control. These reactions can in turn set off a recurring cycle on the service provider's side.

The **Metiv Space - Developing Trauma-Informed Organizations** program works to reduce these harmful incidents and to create a space that does good for trauma survivors, by helping organizations and institutions build a trauma-aware and trauma-informed approach to their organization and their services.

## What is a trauma-informed organization?

A trauma-informed organization is one that understands the impact of trauma on the individual and the community, and accordingly creates a supportive, safe environment and provides service adapted to it. Such an organization:

- **Creates a safe and supportive environment** for employees and clients
- **Pays attention to the service experience** and to preventing renewed traumatic experiences
- **Builds trust** between clients and the organization, and between employees and the organization
- **Addresses burnout and secondary trauma** among employees
- **Breaks the cycle of traumatic reactions** between employees and clients
- **Deals with the effects of collective trauma**
- **Takes part in the recovery and rehabilitation process** of trauma survivors in Israeli society

## What does the training in organizations include?

- Broadening the understanding of trauma and bereavement: symptoms, typical thought patterns, and how these come into play in encounters with service providers and in the workplace
- Organizational change: what needs to be adapted, changed and developed in the organization, according to guiding principles taught in the training
- Developing interpersonal and intrapersonal skills: for personal coping and for providing trauma-informed service
- Tools for coping with states of arousal, aggression, dissociation and the like
